description: OpenAPI path-operation coverage, request-media alternatives, and reverse-direction exclusions.

scenarios.description: A supported path operation remains callable while every request-media declaration and webhook interaction receives its own disposition; the object-schema custom media selects no carriage lane.
A parameter/body-property collision is preserved through a binding-private transform, so both artifact-declared media alternatives remain represented.
A required body property colliding with a parameter remains independently callable and coverage-complete under the current revision.
An absolute sole server makes an ordinary path operation directly invocable without a server-selection prerequisite.
A content-form parameter outside the specification's JSON and text carriage is excluded at synthesis instead of producing an operation that can never faithfully send the declared value.
A document-level custom schema dialect excludes only operations whose projected contracts inherit it; schema-free operations and supported per-schema overrides remain faithfully synthesizable.
A generic OAS 3.0 raw-binary request body is represented for its declared concrete media type without a media-selection requirement.
OAS 3.1 schema-omitted raw bytes and schema-declared encoded text are both represented without collapsing their distinct wire carriage.
A range-only request body remains a represented protocol-blind operation while coverage records the concrete request-media choice required for invocation.
A mixed exact-plus-range request has no target-wide media requirement, while the represented range alternative records the concrete choice it needs.
An optional range-only body has no target-wide requirement because bodyless invocation is available, while its represented range alternative still requires concrete request media.
A declaration-complex exact JSON request remains fully represented through whole-value carriage rather than being excluded by the flattened router.
An exact schema-omitted OAS 3.0 raw-byte operation is fully represented without a media-selection requirement.
An unconstrained multipart part (a bare description with no type) is represented: its OAS per-type part default is keyed by the supplied value's JSON application type at invocation.
A part schema declaring one non-null anyOf branch beside a null branch collapses to that branch's carriage and is represented, while a choice with more than one non-null branch keeps its exclusion.

file.description: The file to process; JSON null elides the part.

scenarios.description: The string-carriage lane needs both halves of a derived scope: a governing schema that resolves to type string, and a media type that is character data. A concrete non-JSON, non-form declaration meeting both is represented -- text/plain, text/csv, and XML alike -- while the same media types declared with an object schema select no lane, because no lane builds a document from an object model. A media type whose registration establishes no character encoding has no defined string-to-octets mapping, so a string-typed binary declaration keeps the byte boundary and is an excluded alternative; under OAS 3.1 format binary carries no assertion force, so that declaration resolves to a bare type string and is decided entirely by its media type. A schema that asserts nothing is the same declaration as an omitted schema and takes the artifact-authorized byte lane.

String content parses under the YAML 1.2.2 grammar pin, and its plain scalars resolve by the core schema's tag resolution: date-shaped, time-shaped and YAML 1.1 boolean-word scalars match none of the null, bool, int or float patterns, so each is a string. The restriction is the artifact authority's, which limits tags to those allowed by YAML's JSON schema ruleset, so no accepted edition carries a timestamp-tagged node. The string-carried document synthesizes exactly as its JSON spelling does.

openapi: 3.0.0
info:
  title: Scalars
  version: 1.0.0
servers:
  - url: https://scalars.example.test
paths:
  /probe:
    get:
      operationId: probe
      parameters:
        - name: issued
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            example: 2020-01-01T12:00:00Z
        - name: day
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            example: 2020-01-01
        - name: at
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            example: 12:30:45
        - name: consent
          in: query
          schema:
            type: string
            example: yes
      responses:
        "200":
          description: ok

scenarios.description: A plain scalar the YAML 1.2.2 core schema resolves to positive infinity has no JSON image, and an OpenAPI document is a JSON object whose YAML spelling exists to round-trip with JSON. The artifact is refused loudly rather than carried with a substituted null the author never wrote.

scenarios.description: A self-recursive component is reached from the request body only through a property the OAS declares readOnly, and from the response body directly. Request projection removes the property, so the emitted input contract must not publish a definition for a component no request instance can contain, while the output contract keeps the same component as its own recursive definition. Both boundaries stay realizable and the operation is fully represented.

JSON Schema 2020-12 defines an array-valued type as a union, so a form part typed ["string", "null"] declares exactly what the collapsing anyOf spelling declares and takes the same carriage: the part is represented, its sibling keywords still apply, and a supplied JSON null elides the optional part. A part typed ["string", "object"] declares two non-null alternatives, leaves no single faithful form carriage, and is an excluded alternative -- the same answer a choice with more than one non-null branch gets. Under the OAS 3.0 line, whose Schema Object requires type to be a string and does not support multiple types via an array, the same union spelling is not a union declaration and its multipart alternative is excluded there too.

A reference cycle closes through a schema position the artifact addresses but does not declare under components.schemas: `#/components/schemas/Wrapper/properties/inner` references itself. The cycle is a cycle wherever it closes, so the emitted operation schema must cut it at the addressed position and stay self-contained; emitting the artifact-space reference into the OBI would publish a reference that does not resolve in the emitted document (OBI-D-16). The operation is realizable and fully represented.

Whether a declared server URL denotes a target address at all decides whether the server configuration point is a runtime prerequisite of the represented target. A sole entry selects itself and, when it resolves, requires nothing. A sole entry whose URL template variable has no Server Variable Object never reduces to a URL -- the OAS substitutes only variables the Server Object declares, and braces appear in no RFC 3986 production -- while a declared variable's REQUIRED default always reduces. A sole entry whose http authority carries no host names no origin server, because RFC 9110 requires a recipient to reject such a URI as invalid. Each of those leaves the target address undetermined, and so does a multi-entry list with no selection, so all three raise configuration.server. Neither answer may be decided by a host language's URL parser: Go's net/url and the WHATWG parser disagree about exactly these two shapes, in opposite directions.
